explanation: Between men, direct eye contact in Saudi Arabia is a normal sign of sincerity and respect. Muslims generally avoid physical contact with the opposite gender, and the same caution extends to eye contact: prolonged eye contact between men and women who are not closely related can be seen as inappropriately forward, so a softer gaze is the safer default in mixed-gender settings.
local_tip: Maintain normal eye contact with people of your own gender; with the opposite gender, keep it brief and polite, especially in business settings.

also_check.note: Prolonged eye contact can feel confrontational; a softer, briefer gaze is preferred.
Direct eye contact is expected as a sign of confidence and honesty in business.
Sustained eye contact with an elder or superior can be read as a challenge rather than respect.
